title: TourGuide Monorepo Structure
intent: Explain how the TourGuide workspace is split across schema, core, TUI, CLI, and legacy Neovim packages.
description: Walks through the package boundaries and data flow in the TourGuide monorepo.

steps.title: Root package wires the monorepo
steps.body: The repository root owns the Bun workspace. `packages/*` is the package boundary, and the root scripts build packages in dependency order: schema, core, TUI, then CLI.

anchors.note: This is the top-level map: workspace packages live under `packages/*`, while root scripts coordinate cross-package build and validation flows.

steps.title: Schema package defines the artifact contract
steps.body: `@tourguide/schema` is the lowest-level package. It exports the JSON contract and validation helpers, and only depends on AJV at runtime.

anchors.note: The package has no dependency on the rest of the monorepo, which keeps the tour format portable.
The schema makes `schemaVersion`, `id`, `title`, and `topics` the required top-level fields for every tour file.

steps.title: Core package normalizes valid tours
steps.body: `@tourguide/core` builds on the schema package. Its main job is to turn valid tour JSON into normalized IDs, flattened steps, and current-step context for renderers or tools.

anchors.note: The dependency edge points from core to schema, not the other way around.
Normalization derives stable topic, step, and anchor IDs while producing a flat `steps` array for navigation.

steps.title: TUI package owns terminal UI screens
steps.body: `@tourguide/tui` depends on core and OpenTUI/Solid. It is where interactive terminal screens live, including the home screen that discovers `.tour.json` files.

anchors.note: The TUI package bridges TourGuide domain data with OpenTUI's Solid renderer.
The current TUI entry point renders `Home`, keeping startup focused on tour selection.
The home screen looks in the working directory and `./tours` for `.tour.json` files before rendering the selectable list.

steps.title: CLI package composes schema, core, and TUI
steps.body: `@tourguide/cli` is the command surface. It validates raw JSON with schema, normalizes valid tours with core, and delegates view rendering to the TUI package.

anchors.note: The dependency list shows the CLI as the top-level package that can import all TourGuide layers.
Each command follows the layer split: validate uses schema, view uses schema plus core plus TUI, and context uses core's normalized step selection.

steps.title: Legacy Neovim package is isolated
steps.body: `packages/tourguide.nvim` is present as a legacy renderer for Lua tours. It is not part of the TypeScript build chain, so changes to the current JSON CLI/TUI path do not need to flow through it.

anchors.note: The package description and single bundle script mark this as a separate legacy surface rather than part of the active TypeScript package graph.

steps.title: Validation starts with strict JSON schema
steps.body: Tour files are strict JSON artifacts. The schema package compiles the JSON schema with AJV and returns either a typed `Tour` or a list of validation issues.

anchors.note: This gives every consumer the same pass/fail contract before any renderer or navigation code touches the tour.

steps.title: Normalized context is the handoff shape
steps.body: After validation, core exposes a compact `StepContext`: tour metadata, the current normalized step, and progress. That is the shape tools can use without re-walking nested topics.

anchors.note: The normalized model keeps topics for grouping but also provides a flat step list for navigation.
`StepContext` is the small, renderer-friendly unit produced by the core layer.
